summary: brief.md covers all eight research steps with ~30 sources: RightNow Media's vendor-stated reach (30K+ churches / 4.5M users, with an unreconciled 20K+ figure on its own pricing page) and a documented absence of any public third-party-content mechanism, closing Part 1's open question as 'no public path, direct ask only'; four denominational/parachurch networks confirmed real but none with a published member count; TGC, Lifeway Leadership Podcast Network, and Christianity Today/SmallGroups.com ad platforms with vendor-stated reach (TGC's 40M claim contradicted by a ~6M/month Similarweb estimate); ChMS ecosystems, where Planning Center's free self-serve developer API plus integrations-directory submission path is the run's clearest actionable-now channel (install base contested at 73K vs. 100K+), Pushpay is partially actionable (API yes, partner program no), and CCB/ChurchTrac/Breeze offer no marketplace; podcasts with only vendor or wide-range estimates and the most on-persona show (Group Answers) unquantified; Part 1's Facebook-groups gap resolved with direct platform reads (SGN 15.2K members/low activity, Small Group Ministry Network 420, Church Communications 38.4K but off-persona); and Apple's generic editorial-featuring process with no faith-specific mechanism. Every channel is classified actionable-now / partially actionable / requires-leverage / too-small, with Planning Center named best actionable-now and RightNow Media best requires-leverage. Overall reliability is moderate-to-low on reach magnitudes: nearly every large number is vendor-stated and single-sourced, two headline figures (RightNow, Planning Center) have internal or cross-source discrepancies, and the headline actionable channel's downstream distribution value is unverified. Five gathering-agent gaps (RightNow direct-ask, no verified small-group-specific podcast/YouTube numbers, unquantified networks, Planning Center count, Google Play unchecked) are carried into Risks and Open questions for critique.
